name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: Who something belongs to — a monitor's owner, an alert's assignee — as a picture or as initials.
docs: Who something belongs to — a monitor's owner, an alert's assignee — as a picture or as initials. ```tsx // initials, when there is no picture // a machine's name works the same way ``` | prop | default | notes | | --------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | `alt` | — | required; a **name**, and it becomes the initials | | `src` | — | omit it, or let it fail, and the initials are used | | `size` | `md` | `sm` 24px, `md` 32px, `lg` 40px | | `color` | `neutral` | `Button`'s five | | `isPreviewable` | `false` | opens the avatar large in a modal; it becomes a button | ## `Avatar.Group` — several of them ```tsx ``` | prop | default | notes | | --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | | `children` | — | the avatars; the ring and the overlap apply to direct children | | `size` | `sm` | `sm` 24px, `md` 32px, `lg` 40px — handed to every avatar inside | | `label` | — | text after the stack; **also the group's accessible name** | | `max` | — | how many to show before the rest are counted as `+N` | | `overflowCount` | — | what the counter says, when the children are not the whole group | | `aria-label` | — | names the group outright, overriding `label` | ### It is `Avatar.Group`, not an `AvatarGroup` **It is not a component that happens to contain avatars — it is what several avatars _are_.** The size it takes, the box it draws, the name it carries and the colour it fills with are all `Avatar`'s, once per face, and the compound form is what says so: a reader who has `Avatar` has `Avatar.Group`. That is the same call `Button.Icon` and `Toolbar.Group` make, and it keeps the library's index of components a list of things rather than a list of arrangements. ### The faces are one object, and the ring is what says so Each avatar covers a **quarter** of the one before it — 18px steps for `sm`, 24 for `md`, 30 for `lg` — and is cut out of it by a 2px ring in the surface the stack is standing on: ```tsx ``` **That ring is the whole trick.** Without it the overlapping faces merge into a smear; with the ring in the wrong colour, it draws a line around a stack that is sitting on something else. `--avatar-ring` is declared on the group and defaults to the page, so a stack inside a panel moves it with one class — the same mechanism `Button`'s colours use, and the reason it is a property rather than a prop. The ring follows the element's own radius, which is the avatar's `rounded-md`: this system squares everything, and a circular cut-out around a square face is what a hand-rolled stack tends to draw. ### `size` travels to the children, and can be overruled The group sizes every avatar inside it through a context of its own, so a stack is sized once rather than at each face — and an avatar that names its own `size` still wins, which is what lets one face in a row be the person the row is about. Its default is `sm`, one step below a lone avatar's `md`: a stack is a summary, not a portrait. `GroupSizes` asserts all three sizes and the exception, by measuring the boxes. ### The counter is the one thing the reference has not got Spectrum's avatar group ends at the avatars and a label. This one counts, because the page it was built for had already invented that by hand — four faces and a hardcoded `+5` in the markup — and a number written into a page is a number nobody maintains. `max` trims the stack; `overflowCount` says what the counter reads when the children are not the whole group, which is the case for any list that arrives a page at a time: three loaded faces out of eight teammates is `max={3} overflowCount={5}`. The counter is a **picture rather than a word**: it reads `+5` and is named "5 more", so a screen reader hears what the eye sees rather than a plus sign. It draws in the avatars' own box at the panel's quieter fill, so the stack stays one height. ### The label is the accessible name A group of faces with no name is an unexplained run of names, so `label` names it: the text is rendered after the stack and wired up as the group's `aria-labelledby`. `aria-label` overrides it, for the group whose visible text is a count or an abbreviation rather than a name. `GroupLabel` asserts both, and that the name really came from the label's own id rather than from a hardcoded string. ## The fourth component with nothing to copy `pulse-replica/` has no avatar, no user chip and nothing person-shaped at all — after the date picker, the accordion and the toast, this is the fourth component here invented rather than replicated. So every decision comes from the system's own language: - **Square by default, and a circle never.** The sheet squares off its controls and makes exactly two exceptions, the checkbox's 2px and the radio's circle; a round avatar would be a **third**, so the box wears the control step of the radius scale — `rounded-md`, which is `0` in the sheet and a soft square under a theme. It is the one place a designer expects a circle, which is why it is stated rather than left to look like an oversight. - **A fill carrying `ink`**, like every other filled control: black on the luminous dark-theme accents, white on the deep light-theme ones. The five colours are literally `Button`'s table, so an avatar cannot drift away from the palette it sits beside. - **Mono, uppercase, letterspaced initials** — the face every other label here wears. ## Initials are derived, and the edges are checked The first letter of the first and last words, or the first two letters of a single word: | `alt` | initials | | ----------------- | -------- | | `Ada Lovelace` | `AL` | | `Ada B. Lovelace` | `AL` | | `fra1` | `FR` | | `" "` | `?` | A middle name does not change it, because the surname is what distinguishes two Adas. A name with no letters at all still has to render something, so it gets `?` rather than an empty box — the one case where the fallback invents rather than derives. A generic silhouette was the alternative and was rejected: it says "somebody", and in a monitoring system _which_ somebody is the entire content of the cell. ## A broken image falls back to initials, not to nothing `onError` swaps the `` for the initials. This is not an edge case — an avatar URL that 404s, a service with no picture, a directory that has not synced — it is the state a real dashboard spends most of its life in, and the failure mode of not handling it is an empty box. `BrokenImage` is a story with a source that cannot load, and it asserts the initials appear and the `` is gone. ## The name is announced once The wrapper is `role="img"` with `aria-label={alt}` and the inner `` is `alt=""`. Giving both a name announces the same person twice; giving only the image one leaves the initials case — the majority case — with no name at all. The `Default` story asserts the picture **actually arrived** by checking `naturalWidth`: an `` in the DOM proves nothing on its own, because a 404 leaves one behind. ## `isPreviewable` changes the element, not the styling ```tsx ``` Off — the default — this is a ``, a picture the tab order correctly skips. On, it is a **real `
